_comment_mutate: src/lib takes .tsx as well as .ts. The four React context files there were never deliberately excluded; the .ts-only glob simply never reached them, leaving ThemeContext.tsx unmeasured despite its 319-line test file. constants-generated.ts is machine-written from api/pkg/constants and its correctness property is parity with that source, which the Go test api/scripts/generate-ts-constants_test.go asserts directly: it drives the generator's own collectConstants and generateTSOutput over api/pkg/constants/constants.go and holds the committed artifact byte for byte against the result, so a changed value, a renamed constant, an added or dropped constant, or a hand edit fails go test rather than mutation. techniques.ts and themes.ts stay excluded on a measurement, not a hunch: 96% of techniques.ts's 3144 mutants are static (module-level data), Stryker's own estimate for one shard was ~53 hours, and every one of the 13 mutants that did run returned Timeout, which the aggregate scores as caught. Admitting it whole would report thousands of clock-kills as assertion-kills. Their genuine logic (207 mutants across query, glossary and colour-derivation functions) is being split into separately mutated modules instead.
_comment_thresholds: high/low are display thresholds (the portal reads them for its ok/warn coloring); 'break' is deliberately absent. A break threshold here was a second, independent gate at 90 while the real floors live in api/mutation-floors.json (hooks 100, surface 97), which is the two-sources problem. The enforcing gate is each scope's aggregate job in nightly-mutation.yml, which reads its floor from that file, and every shard step already runs continue-on-error because the aggregate is the scope's gate. Do not reintroduce break without deleting the aggregate gates.
_comment_dryRunTimeoutMinutes: Bounds one thing only: the single initial test run Stryker performs before any mutant is tested. It is not the mutation phase's budget; each mutant's own run is bounded separately by timeoutMS (5000 ms) and timeoutFactor (1.5), both left at their defaults, and it is those per-mutant limits, not this ceiling, that produce the Timeout kills. The value is measured, not assumed: across all 77 shards of hosted run 34928015321 the slowest initial test run took 90 seconds (median 84), and the same suite (2895 tests at local head f442807) measured locally at 4 minutes 08 seconds, or 8 minutes 28 under heavy concurrent load, so 20 minutes is roughly 13x the worst hosted shard and still 2.4x the most contended local measurement: a genuinely hung initial run fails in a third of an hour instead of two. It is deliberately unequal to both containing job timeouts in nightly-mutation.yml (surface 120, hooks 90): when the ceiling and a job timeout shared a number, a cancellation could not say which limit had fired.
_comment_ignorePatterns: Report artifact directories, none of which the tests read. Local allure-results alone holds ~422k files: unignored, ProjectReader spends ~100s walking them and the sandbox copy exhausts a tmpfs. A CI checkout is clean, so this matters for local iteration and costs CI nothing.
